description: Manual account checks that have no API. S13-github-npm.ps1 copies every item into inventory.manualChecks, resolves {placeholders} (githubUser, npmUser, npmPackage, gateway) and evaluates 'when' so each item says whether this machine shows evidence the account/service is in use. Conditions: always | sshKeyNameRegex | expectedId | expectedHostRegex | knownHostsRegex | pathExists | gitEmailDomainRegex. Edit freely; no collector change needed.

items.title: Active web sessions
lookFor: Sessions from devices, browsers, countries or IPs you do not recognise
Revoke anything unknown, then change the password

items.title: Security log (account audit trail)
lookFor: oauth_authorization.create: OAuth apps you did not authorise (a GitHub CLI authorisation created for this scanner's signed-in checks is expected)
personal_access_token.* and oauth_access.create: tokens you did not create
public_key.create / gpg_key.create: SSH or GPG keys you did not add
two_factor_authentication.*: 2FA disabled, recovery codes viewed/regenerated, new 2FA methods
repo.create / repo.access: new repos, or private repos switched to public (Shai-Hulud '-migration', s1ngularity)
user.login and new-device events: logins from new IPs or countries

items.title: Authorised OAuth apps
lookFor: Unknown apps
Apps with repo, workflow, admin:org, delete_repo or write:packages scopes you do not use
Recently authorised apps

items.title: Authorised and installed GitHub Apps
lookFor: Unknown GitHub Apps
Apps installed on all repositories that only need a few
Apps with write access to code, workflows or secrets

items.title: Personal access tokens (classic and fine-grained)
lookFor: Tokens you do not recognise
Tokens with no expiry
Recent 'last used' on tokens you no longer use
A classic token stored in plaintext in a user .npmrc (for example for npm.pkg.github.com): keep only if needed, give it read:packages only, set an expiry

items.title: 2FA, passkeys, SSH/GPG keys and emails
lookFor: 2FA enabled with an authenticator app or security key (not SMS only)
Unknown passkeys or security keys
Recovery codes stored offline
SSH/GPG/signing keys you cannot map to one of your devices
Email addresses you did not add (an attacker email enables password resets)

items.title: npm access tokens
lookFor: Tokens you do not recognise
Write (publish) tokens without expiry or CIDR restriction
Recently created tokens
If a user .npmrc holds a plaintext token, replace it with a short-lived granular token (or trusted publishing) and revoke the old one

items.title: npm 2FA, account and package publishing access
lookFor: 2FA mode 'authorization and writes' (or security-key only)
Packages you do not recognise under your account
Publishing access set to 'Require two-factor authentication and disallow tokens' (or trusted publishing only)
Maintainers you did not add

items.title: Tailscale admin console
lookFor: Unknown devices or devices shared in from other tailnets
Devices with key expiry disabled
Reusable or long-lived auth keys
Configuration audit log entries you did not make (ACL changes, new users, Funnel/Serve)

items.title: Microsoft account recent activity
lookFor: Successful sign-ins from unknown locations or apps
Unknown devices
Security info (phone/email/authenticator) you did not add
Apps with access you no longer use

items.title: Google security checkup
lookFor: Recent security events you did not cause
Unknown signed-in devices
Third-party apps with Gmail/Drive access
Gmail forwarding addresses or filters that forward or delete mail

items.title: Anthropic Console / Claude account
lookFor: API keys you do not recognise or with unexpected 'last used'
Unknown organisation members or invites
Usage spikes you did not cause
Unknown active sessions and connectors on claude.ai

items.title: Your servers ({hosts})
lookFor: In the hosting provider's control panel: account activity, 2FA, API tokens, firewall and snapshot changes you did not make
On the server: ~/.ssh/authorized_keys of every user (compare fingerprints with the local keys listed in context)
/var/log/auth.log (or journalctl -u ssh): 'Accepted' logins from unknown IPs; last -i; new users in /etc/passwd; unknown crontab entries; unexpected listening ports (ss -tlnp)

items.title: Cloud provider console (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud or another)
lookFor: IAM: users, service accounts, access keys and API keys you did not create
VMs or GPU instances you did not start (crypto-mining)
SSH keys on VMs you cannot map to a local key
Audit logs and billing anomalies

items.title: Mail on your own domain: forwarding rules, filters and sessions
lookFor: In the mail provider's webmail/admin for each mailbox: forwarding addresses, filters/rules that forward, hide or delete mail, auto-replies
App passwords and active sessions
Admin panel: new mailboxes, aliases or catch-all forwards you did not create

items.title: Router admin page ({gateway})
lookFor: DNS servers: must be your ISP's or ones you chose (changed DNS = hijack)
Firmware: latest version from the vendor
Remote (WAN) management: off
UPnP: off, or review its port mappings
WPS: off
Admin password changed from the default
Unknown DHCP clients and port forwards
